producer_report.summary:
I wrote docs/design/warm-baseline-build.md from scratch (the file did not exist in this copy) and added a CHANGELOG entry. The note contradicts the review's reading of the 14.1 minutes. The review window ran almost all its checks locally, so the 14.1 minutes is mostly the local path, not CI wait. The note recommends against building the warm baseline now.

**What the note says:**
- **Existing code:** a table lists the CI-first flow and polling up to ci_wait_s, the local fallback, the target-cache restore on every event, and the 6-shard test job. Each row names its file and function or step and is tagged "already present".
- **Per-path numbers:**
  - CI runs: median 583 s (9.7 min), range 400 to 690 s, from 53 recorded `CI run <id> (<n>s)` lines.
  - Local runs: October window 14.1 min, from the review. November median 18.5 min for fmt, clippy and test together, from six local verification records.
- **Local share:** the review window had 393 verification records, 4 of which reused CI, so about 99 percent ran locally. From 2026-10-29 16:00 to 2026-10-31, 12 of 41 reused. November had 51 of 59 reused, so 8 ran locally (about 14 percent).
- **Correction:** the false "mostly CI wait" claim is replaced. The next review's comparison with 14.1 must be split by CI versus local.
- **Freshness:** stable Cargo uses file mtimes, so workspace crates rebuild and only third-party dependencies are reused.
- **Scaled prediction:** the 8.0-minute estimate becomes about 1.1 minutes per landed job at most, or about 0.6 after the freshness correction (estimate). The note says most jobs would not benefit.
- **Recommendation:** every item is tagged. Restoring the target cache on pull-request runs and splitting test are marked "already present". The rest are new: record why a job fell back to local, split local test time into build and run, don't build the baseline now, and an optional per-shard cache key.
- **Alternatives:** the note compares no change, a warm local baseline, extending the CI path, the CI target cache, a shared target dir, and sccache.
- **Next review:** the note cites review 20261029-155931-wfkr and sets out how the next review measures the saving.

criteria_check.evidence: Section 1 of the note is a table. Its rows cite routing.rs (route, run_routed_with_record, CI_POLL, ci_polls, Paced, Fallback, run_local, NoCi), ci.yml (the 'Restore the target cache' step and the test shard matrix), and ci-routing.md sections 4.1 and 4.4. I read all three files first.

criteria_check.criterion: The Problem section gives measured durations for the CI-reuse path (median of the recorded 'CI run <id> (<n>s)' durations in brief-verifier records) and the local-run path (from verification.json records and THROUGHPUT.md), each number with its source or an 'estimate' label, and states the local-run share both for the review window (279 landings up to 2026-10-29, mostly local) and for November (about 50 of 58 reused CI).
criteria_check.evidence: Section 2.1 gives the CI median of 583 s from 53 grep-matched lines, and the local medians from 6 verification.json files, each with its source. THROUGHPUT.md is absent from this working copy, so the review record supplies the 14.1-minute October figure and the note cites that instead. Section 2.2 counts 393 records with 4 reused up to the review and 59 records with 51 reused in November. The snapshot has grown since the brief's '50 of 58', so I report 51 of 59.

criteria_check.criterion: The note checks the claim that the 14.1-minute median is mostly CI wait against the records, and corrects it: the October review window ran checks mostly locally, and the later bounded CI polling (job 20261101-061448-sdya) already moved the stage away from 14.1; the note says the next review's comparison to 14.1 must be split by CI versus local.
criteria_check.evidence: Section 2.3 says the first attempt's claim is wrong because about 99 percent of the window ran locally. It credits the polling from job 20261101-061448-sdya with moving the stage and says the comparison with 14.1 must be split by CI versus local.

criteria_check.criterion: Every recommendation is tagged 'new' or 'already present'; none re-proposes restoring the target cache on pull-request runs or splitting test across jobs, which ci.yml and ci-routing.md already do. The remaining recommendation follows the measured cause, scales the 8.0-minute prediction to the local-fallback share, and says plainly if most jobs would not benefit.
criteria_check.evidence: Section 6 tags item 1 'already present' and items 2 to 5 'new'. Section 4 scales 8.0 by the 14 percent local share to 1.1 minutes per landed job at most (about 0.6 after the freshness correction, estimate), and says 'most jobs would not benefit'.

criteria_check.criterion: Alternatives considered include a warm local baseline, warming or extending the CI-result path and CI target cache, shared target dir, sccache and no change, compared with reasons; the note corrects the freshness claim (stable Cargo uses file mtimes, workspace crates rebuild, only third-party deps reuse).
criteria_check.evidence: The section 5 table has all six options, each with a reason. Section 3 states the mtime and workspace-crate rebuild correction.

criteria_check.criterion: The note cites review 20261029-155931-wfkr and states how the next throughput review measures the saving (median minutes per landed job over the last 20, checks stage versus 14.1 and 25.4, split by CI versus local).
criteria_check.evidence: The header and section 7 cite the review. Section 7 gives the median over the last 20 landings, the checks stage against 14.1 and the whole against 25.4, split by CI versus local using the verification.json 'reused' field.

criteria_check.criterion: git diff shows changes only to docs/design/warm-baseline-build.md and CHANGELOG.md; rust-toolchain.toml, athena.toml, defaults.toml, Cargo.lock, crates/, xtask/ and .github/workflows/ are unchanged.
criteria_check.evidence: git status --short lists only ' M CHANGELOG.md' and '?? docs/design/warm-baseline-build.md'.

open_issues: The records do not say why 8 of 59 November jobs fell back to local checks. The note recommends recording the reason as a new follow-up job.
The 4 CI reuses before the review (all in October) were not explained, and the note says so.
The 18.5-minute November local median rests on 6 jobs. It is higher than 14.1, probably because of job mix (estimate, untested).
The roughly 4-minute saving per local run after the freshness correction is an estimate, labeled as one.
mistakes: I counted 53 CI run durations; the brief and the earlier verifier said 52. The snapshot has since gained a job, and the note says n = 53.
Two of the 8 November jobs that did not reuse CI were not read, so their local durations and fallback reasons are unknown. The note states this.
learnings: CI reuse covers whole jobs: verification.json has 'reused': true on each reused check, and a reused check records duration 0.0 with basis 'recorded result'. The CI wait therefore does not show in the checks-stage duration.

The evidence snapshot has 434 October and 59 November verification.json files, and 53 brief-verifier lines of the form 'CI run <id> (<n>s)'. Both are larger than the earlier counts (52 CI runs, 58 November files), because the snapshot is newer.
Local November fmt, clippy and test took 953 to 1248 s per job. Clippy took only 34 to 39 s and test took about 17.8 minutes, so compile may not be the bulk of the test check (not measured).
ci.yml and ci-routing.md section 4.4 already document that the six test shards share one target-test cache key and only shard 0 saves it.
desires: THROUGHPUT.md is absent from the producer copy; a per-path duration table in it would have been easier to cite.
A records-side summary of why each job ran checks locally; the records do not say.
